I am 65 years old and have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou for 20 years. I finished high school, so I can read the agricultural extension bulletins from the county station, but I also trust what my own eyes tell me after two decades on this land. My household has 10 people—my wife, children, and grandchildren. Some of my children work off-farm in Handan or Shijiazhuang and send money home, but they come back for planting and harvest, so labor is not a problem. I have my own well, so I can irrigate when I need to, though I try not to waste electricity.

This year I will stick with my wheat-maize double crop on all 8 mu. It is the only system that makes sense on the North China Plain. The wheat season starts now in autumn. I will do rotary tillage to prepare a fine seedbed, then sow an improved wheat variety at about 15 kg per mu. For fertilizer, I will apply compound fertilizer as a basal dose and then topdress with urea at green-up and jointing. I know the county technicians say farmers here use too much nitrogen, so I try to be careful—I aim for about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, plus 6 kg of phosphorus and 5 kg of potassium. I will irrigate three times: winter irrigation to protect the seedlings from the cold, then at jointing, and once more at flowering if the spring is dry. Two sprays should be enough—herbicide early, and a fungicide only if I see disease. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

After wheat harvest in early June, there is no time to waste before the autumn frost. I will plant hybrid maize seed directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. The growing season is short, and no-tillage saves time and keeps soil moisture. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress with urea later. I give maize slightly less total fertilizer than wheat—about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice: once at tasseling, and again during grain filling if the summer is dry. Herbicide and one insecticide spray for the corn borer. I expect around 550 kg per mu. I do not chase maximum yield because my children send remittances, and my goal is steady production without big risks or wasted inputs.
